One of the most important aspects in troubleshooting electronic equipment is to know that the input signal is correct.
With no input to the antenna, you would not expect to hear music from the speaker.
Function Generators are used to produce a known input, so the technician can test the circuit.
A Doctor uses known input sounds to check a patients hearing ability.
A Technician uses known input signals to check a circuits ability to operate..........
Let's begin the lesson on INTRODUCTION TO THE FUNCTION GENERATOR............
Function Generators are part of a large group of tools called
ELECTRONIC TEST EQUIPMENT - Electronic test equipment is designed to measure or test specific functions in electronic circuits. A few types of test equipment are:
The function generator is a tool used to produce accurate AC
These AC signals are then used as inputs to circuits. With a known input, circuit values can be calculated, measured, and checked.
A display is used to indicate the frequency of the output signal.
Controls and switches are used to select and modify the output signal.
The function generator produces these types of waveforms:
The frequency of the chosen output signal is adjustable from less than 1 Hz to tens of MHz.
The amplitude of the output signal is adjustable from less than 1 mVpp to 10 Vpp.
The amount of DC voltage added to the AC waveform is adjustable up to +10 volts.
The symmetry of the output signal is adjustable.
SYMMETRY - Symmetry is an exact correspondence between the opposite halves of a figure or pattern. Half of something is the mirror image of the other half. This sine wave is symmetrical.
The symmetry of the output signal is adjustable.
The output signal can also be modulated.
AM or FM modulation using sine, square, or triangle signals are available. Input Signal Modulating Signal OutputSignal Amplitude-

MODULATED - The term modulate means to change or regulate the intensity, pitch, amplitude, frequency, or tone. A low frequency signal is often used to modulate the output signal (modulating signal). The high frequency signal is called the carrier. Radio and television use modulated signals...
The output signal can also be modulated.
AM or FM modulation using sine, square, or triangle signals are available. Input Signal Modulating Signal OutputSignal Amplitude-
AM - AM is the abbreviation for Amplitude Modulation. The amplitude of the carrier signal is changed using a low frequency modulating signal. AM radio uses amplitude modulation.
FM - FM is the abbreviation for Frequency Modulation. The frequency of the carrier signal is changed by the low frequency modulating signal. FM radio uses frequency modulation.

Function Generators have three major sections:
The frequency section selects the type of signal, frequency,
amplitude, DC offset, CMOS level and duty cycle (symmetry) of the output. +
This section consists of the function, range, and output level (amplitude) controls. There are two outputs and three inputs, the VCG/MOD is for external modulation.
The FUNCTION switches select the type of signal output:
The duty cycle (symmetry) control changes the waveform. For example, a triangle wave can be changed to a ramp or the square wave to a pulse.
When you push in a Range button, the Display will show a frequency. The Coarse and Fine control knobs vary the frequency within the selected Range button and the previous Range button value...

For Range buttons from 2 through 2k, the Display shows the frequency in Hz. For Range buttons 20k and above you must multiply the Display by 1000 Hz, because it is displayed in kHz. multipliers for the FREQUENCY dial. The range is from .1 Hz to
The DISPLAY indicates the frequency in 10ths of hertz to over 20 MHz. It is a frequency counter. nter.
The numbers above the Range Buttons show you the automatic Gate select for each range. These numbers tell you how often the display is updated.
The INT/EXT (internal/external) button, selects which input frequency is displayed.....
When INT/EXT button is out, the display indicates the frequency of the signal produced inside the function generator.
When the INT/EXT button is pushed in, it displays the frequency of a signal produced from an outside source connected to the EXT counter BNC.
The Output Level Control knob and the -20 dB button sets the amplitude and attenuation of the internally generated output signal.
The DC Offset button and the DC Offset Control knob sets the amount of DC voltage the AC signal rides on. With the DC Offset button, in the out position, no DC voltage is applied.
The Duty Cycle Button and Duty Cycle Control knob varies the symmetry of the output waveform. With the button in the out position, the signal is symmetrical.
The Burst Button and Burst Width Control knob set the trigger phase starting point of the output signal. With the Burst Button in the out position the signal is in the Free Run Mode.
The output waveform is taken from the output BNC.
The SYNC output BNC is used for synchronizing other test equipment, such as an oscilloscope.
